supported_findings.evidence: Full regression coef 2.03, p~5e-252; holdout with X1,X2,X3 gives test R2 0.765.
Coef 0.181, p=1.5e-5 in full regression; small effect, adds little holdout R2 (0.772 vs 0.765 with X5).
Coef 0.147, p=0.0004 in full regression; small effect.

Holdout test R2 jumped from 0.772 (X1-X5) to 0.877 when adding X2:X5 and X4:X5, while other interaction sets did not help; likely at least one of these products is a real effect, though which one is not isolated.
Same holdout jump (test R2 0.877 vs 0.772); the contribution cannot be separated from X2:X5 with the calls used.

interaction_claims.reason: Interaction p=0.104, delta R2 0.0018; not significant.
Holdout with X1:X4, X1:X5, X2:X4, X3:X4, X3:X5 did not improve test R2 (0.767 vs 0.772).

Adding X2:X5 and X4:X5 raised holdout test R2 substantially (0.772 to 0.877), consistent across train, so out-of-sample improvement. Not individually tested, so attribution between X2:X5 and X4:X5 is uncertain.
Part of the same holdout gain; it could come from X2:X5, X4:X5, or both, and was not tested separately.

causal_claims.reason: Observational regression and holdout fit show strong association only; no causal identification.
Strong negative association; no design to establish causality.
